item.text:
## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix the finish-time calculation before merge because it reports a finish time for a process whose only event is a start.

## Changes

The pull request adds and documents a `finished_at` column in the current-state model, which still selects one row per process from its latest event.

## Critical

- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Populate `finished_at` from a completion event — Process 20 has only a `started` event, yet the model emits its start time as `finished_at`. The source permits `created`, `started`, and `cleared`, and the expression only returns a timestamp for `started`. — Consumers can treat a process that has only started as already finished. — Fix: Define which source event represents completion and use its timestamp.

## Important

- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Document when `finished_at` is null — Process 30 has a `started` event followed by a `cleared` event, yet `finished_at` is null. “NULL means the process has never been started” contradicts `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end`, which evaluates only the latest event. — Consumers who use null to identify never-started processes will misclassify processes that started and were later cleared.

## Suggestions

- models/processes.sql:10 — tests — Test that a created-only process has no finish time — Process 10 has only a `created` event, and the fixture contains no assertion that its `finished_at` stays null. — A regression that assigns a finish time to a never-started process would go undetected.
